sentences: Of all the changes that have taken place in English-language newspapers during the past quarter-century perhaps the most far-reaching has been the inexorable decline in the scope and seriousness of their arts coverage.
It is difficult to the point of impossibility for the average reader under the age of forty to imagine a time when high-quality arts criticism could be found in most big-city newspapers.
Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews.
To read such books today is to marvel at the fact that their learned contents were once deemed suitable for publication in general-circulation dailies.
translations: 在过去的四分之一世纪里，英语报纸上发生的所有变化中，影响最为深远的或许就是其艺术报道的范围和严肃性不可阻挡地缩减了。
对于年龄在四十岁以下的普通读者来说，几乎无法想象一个能在大多数大城市报纸上找到高质量艺术评论的时代。
然而，在20世纪出版的相当数量的重要评论集中，很大一部分是由报纸评论组成的。
今天阅读这样的书，会让人惊叹于这样一个事实：它们那博学的内容曾被认为适合刊登在面向大众发行的日报上。

sentences: We are even farther removed from the unfocused newspaper reviews published in England between the turn of the 20th century and the eve of World War II, at a time when newsprint was dirt-cheap and stylish arts criticism was considered an ornament to the publications in which it appeared.
In those far-off days, it was taken for granted that the critics of major papers would write in detail and at length about the events they covered.
Theirs was a serious business, and even those reviewers who wore their learning lightly, like George Bernard Shaw and Ernest Newman, could be trusted to know what they were about.
These men believed in journalism as a calling, and were proud to be published in the daily press.

"So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism," Newman wrote, "that I am tempted to define 'journalism' as 'a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are'."
translations: 我们距离20世纪初至二战前夕在英国发表的、主题松散的报纸评论甚至更远了，那时新闻纸极其便宜，时髦的艺术评论被视为其所在出版物的装饰。
在那个遥远的年代，人们理所当然地认为，主要报纸的评论家会详尽而充分地报道他们所涉及的事件。
他们从事的是严肃的事业，即使是那些学识渊博却不炫耀的评论家，如乔治·萧伯纳和欧内斯特·纽曼，也可以放心他们会清楚自己在做什么。
这些人相信新闻业是一种天职，并为能在日报上发表文章而感到自豪。
“很少有作家有足够的头脑或文学天赋在新闻业中坚持到底，”纽曼写道，“以至于我想把‘新闻业’定义为‘一个由无人阅读的作家用来形容拥有读者的作家的轻蔑术语’。”

sentences: Unfortunately, these critics are virtually forgotten.
Neville Cardus, who wrote for the Manchester Guardian from 1917 until shortly before his death in 1975, is now known solely as a writer of essays on the game of cricket.
During his lifetime, though, he was also one of England's foremost classical-music critics, and a stylist so widely admired that his Autobiography (1947) became a best-seller.
He was knighted in 1967, the first music critic to be so honored.
Yet only one of his books is now in print, and his vast body of writings on music is unknown save to specialists.
translations: 不幸的是，这些评论家几乎被遗忘了。
内维尔·卡德斯，从1917年起直到1975年去世前不久一直为《曼彻斯特卫报》撰稿，如今仅以撰写板球比赛散文的作家而闻名。
然而，在他生前，他也是英国最重要的古典音乐评论家之一，并且是一位备受推崇的文体家，他的《自传》（1947年）因此成为畅销书。
他于1967年被封为爵士，是第一位获此殊荣的音乐评论家。
然而，他的书现在只有一本仍在印行，他大量的音乐评论作品除了专家之外无人知晓。

sentences: Is there any chance that Cardus's criticism will enjoy a revival?
The prospect seems remote.
Journalistic tastes had changed long before his death, and postmodern readers have little use for the richly upholstered Vicwardian prose in which he specialized.
Moreover, the amateur tradition in music criticism has been in headlong retreat.
translations: 卡德斯的评论是否有可能复兴？
前景似乎渺茫。
在他去世前很久，新闻品味就已经改变了，后现代读者对他所擅长的华丽装饰的维多利亚-爱德华时代散文几乎不感兴趣。
此外，音乐评论中的业余传统一直在急速衰退。

sentences:
23. Which of the following would Shaw and Newman most probably agree on?
A. It is writers' duty to fulfill journalistic goals.
B. It is contemptible for writers to be journalists.
C. Writers are likely to be tempted into journalism.
D. Not all writers are capable of journalistic writing.
translations:

A. 实现新闻目标是作家的职责。
B. 作家成为记者是可鄙的。
C. 作家很可能被诱惑进入新闻业。
D. 并非所有作家都能胜任新闻写作。

sentences:

D. His writings fail to follow the amateur tradition.
translations:

B. 他作为音乐评论家的声誉长期以来一直存在争议。
C. 他的风格主要迎合现代专家。
D. 他的作品未能遵循业余传统。
